Chelsea women's side remain unbeaten as they chase form under new coach

29 Oct 2026, 08:37 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Chelsea have kept a perfect unbeaten record across all competitions this season, topping the Women's Super League with Manchester City after seven matches. In the Champions League group stage they have won two games and drawn one of their opening three fixtures, with a 2‑0 victory over Roma on Wednesday. The win, secured by substitute Ellie Carpenter and defender Kadeisha Buchanan, marked another step in a campaign that has seen the Blues build on a domestic treble in Sonia Bompastor’s first year in charge.

Current Form and Achievements

The team is currently unbeaten in every competition, sitting at the top of the WSL standings. Their Champions League run includes a 2‑0 win over Roma, a 3‑1 defeat to Austria Vienna and a 1‑1 draw with Barcelona in the group stage. The unbeaten run in the league phase means they are the only side to start the season without a loss, a record that places them ahead of Manchester City after seven games.

Manager’s Comments

Sonia Bompastor said the results are “really pleased” and highlighted the importance of a solid defensive base. “We have played three games and we haven’t conceded,” she added. She noted that the Champions League is a different level from the WSL and that the squad has been rotated effectively to handle the demands of both competitions. Bompastor also stressed the need for mental and cultural cohesion, stating that “the way we are performing gives us a really good advantage and a big chance to win games.”

Player Highlights

Key contributors include full‑back Ellie Carpenter, who has four goals in all competitions, and England forward Lauren James, who is in scintillating form. Midfielder Lexi Potter is developing a flourishing partnership with Lionesses star Keira Walsh. Defender Kadeisha Buchanan’s clinical defending has been a highlight, and goalkeeper Hannah Hampton’s distribution has helped the team adapt between a back three and a back four.

Context and Challenges

The unbeaten start follows a period of transition after the departure of big‑name players such as Sam Kerr, Millie Bright and Guro Reiten. Bompastor acknowledged that the club is still adjusting to a new coach and a new playing philosophy, describing it as a “transition period” that requires time for players to adapt. Despite the changes, the squad has shown resilience, maintaining a high level of performance despite the loss of experienced players.
